A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same StaMo work, with matching methods, equations and retained results. v1 includes Appendices A–C; supplied v2 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix. This observable omission can be assessed alongside the retained and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, LIBERO policy evaluation, co-training, action-probing and real-robot results, plus appendix ablations and action-replay experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative ManiSkill transfer and planning evaluations, expanded comparisons and a decoder-pretraining ablation.

M1.justification: The core encoder, state-difference motion representation and training objectives remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 4.2 newly describes replacing the original VLA vision encoders with StaMo, whereas v1 describes attaching a prediction head. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents an implementation change or newly disclosed detail.

E1.justification: v2 adds executed-policy zero-shot transfer and goal-conditioned planning on four ManiSkill manipulation tasks. v1 used ManiSkill for out-of-domain image reconstruction and demonstrated goal-to-action replay on LIBERO-10. This substantially extends evaluated task requirements; simulation, DROID, OXE and egocentric training coverage already existed.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 expands the LIBERO comparison with DP, Octo-Base, Spatial-VLA, CoT-VLA, pi0-FAST, WorldVLA and DINOv2-feature controls. It also adds real-world comparator rows, broader speed comparisons and DINO-WM for goal-conditioned planning. The ATM/LAPA co-training comparisons and probing comparator set remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New ManiSkill protocols use 100 trials per task for zero-shot deployment and frozen-encoder goal-conditioned planning. The OFT reference changes from a wrist-camera-free reproduction in v1 Table 3 to an explicitly unmodified baseline in v2 Table 2. v2 also introduces a decoder-initialization control. These are substantive evaluation-design additions and configuration changes.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative environment-transfer testing, DINOv2-feature controls and a pretrained-versus-scratch decoder ablation. Conversely, it omits the additional appendix interpolation/transfer visualizations and LIBERO-10 action-replay analysis. The token-dimension ablation is retained unchanged as Table 8, and the existing data-scaling analysis is reorganized rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 Appendices A–B disclose seed 33 and shared seeds for probing-data sampling and splitting; these disclosures are absent from v2. Both versions retain co-training averages over three full runs. Neither reports confidence intervals or significance tests, and no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: LIBERO results are revised: OpenVLA and its StaMo-state variant report averages of 71.7% and 86.0% in v1 Table 3, versus 76.5% and 87.6% in v2 Table 2. Changed or incompletely matched configurations prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. v2 adds transfer, planning, speed and decoder-ablation results and replaces the real-world comparison table. Reconstruction, co-training, probing and token-dimension scores remain unchanged; scaling averages survive in Figure 6.

T1.justification: The flow-matching objective, state-difference formulation, combined policy loss and probing equations are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The compact-state, emergent-motion and scalable co-training contributions remain intact. Headline gains change from 14.3% to 11.6% on LIBERO and from 30% to 31% in real-world tasks. The conclusion replaces generalization to unseen robots with the less embodiment-specific claim of generalization to unseen scenarios.

C2.justification: v2 attributes transfer performance to retaining manipulation-relevant information, dimensional robustness to the decoder's generative prior, and the new ablation outcome to natural-image pretraining. It omits v1 Appendix B's precise-grasping failure explanation involving insufficient gripper descent. The interpretation that motion versus state targets suit different action horizons is retained.

D1.justification: v2 omits extensive appendix documentation: optimizer settings, learning rate, batch size, training hardware/time, approximately 20,000 probing samples, the 95/5 split, probe architecture, robot control frequency and action conventions. It newly specifies RTX 4090 timing hardware, 1,000 LIBERO rollouts per task and the EgoVid-5M source. These additions do not replace the missing implementation detail; appendix references remain unresolved within supplied v2.

R1.justification: The related-work organization and principal positioning remain largely intact. v2 adds citations for comparison methods, datasets and additional VLA research. It removes MovieDreamer and the explicit acknowledgment in the introduction and method section that Zhao et al. inspired the diffusion-autoencoder approach.

P1.justification: Most introductory, related-work and methodological prose is retained, with wording, heading and affiliation edits. v2 separates speed and scaling discussions into dedicated subsections, moves the dimensionality discussion into the main ablation section, and omits the standalone ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column preprint layout to two columns, substantially resizing and rearranging figures and tables. v2 expands comparison-table structures, adds transfer/planning/decoder-ablation tables, relocates the dimensionality table from the appendix, and omits appendix Figures 7–9. Retained probing and scaling plots are redisplayed rather than new results.

improvement.justification: The new quantitative transfer/planning tests, broader comparisons and decoder ablation strengthen evidence for generalization and design choices. However, v2 loses substantial training, probing and robot-protocol documentation and the concrete grasping-failure discussion, while referring to an unavailable appendix. Its newly described encoder replacement also complicates interpreting revised benchmark results. These empirical gains and reproducibility losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
